```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

library(mia)
library(magrittr)
library(tidyverse)
library(parkinsonsMetagenomicData)
library(ggtext)

library(ggpubr)
library(meta)

# for table visualizations
library(DT)
library(kableExtra)

library(biobakeryUtils)
theme_set(theme_bw())

# create base directory output
outdir <- sprintf("SupplementaryFigures")
dir.create(outdir, recursive = TRUE)

pd_color_palette <- c("Control" = "gray60", "PD" = "#EBA07EFF")

# generate an incremental figure index
suppFigIndx <- 1
```

```{r prepare data for plot}
Input.tse <- read_TSE_from_dir(sprintf("~/parkinsonMetaAnalysis_data/03-analysis_ready_datasets/01-dataset_complete-%s.tse", params$biobakery_tool))

# Parkinson as target condition
Input_parkinson.tse <- Input.tse[, Input.tse$target_condition == "Parkinson Disease"]
Input_parkinson.tse <- Input_parkinson.tse[rowSums(assay(Input_parkinson.tse)) > 0, ]

# drop unused level of the parkinson_for_analysis
Input_parkinson.tse$parkinson_for_analysis <- droplevels(Input_parkinson.tse$parkinson_for_analysis)

# Each dataset should have at least 10 samples in cases and 10 in controls
# (same rule as 02-Analyses/03-PD-metaAnalysis.qmd)
ok_datasets <- Input_parkinson.tse@colData %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  group_by(study_name) %>%
  filter(
    sum(parkinson_for_analysis == "Control") >= 10,
    sum(parkinson_for_analysis == "PD") >= 10
  )

## filter TSE to restrict to 'ok' datasets 
Input_parkinson_usableDatasets.tse <- Input_parkinson.tse[,Input_parkinson.tse$study_name %in% unique(ok_datasets$study_name)]

# prepare data for plot "reads per dataset color by PD status"
data_for_plot.df <- as.data.frame(colData(Input_parkinson_usableDatasets.tse)) %>% 
  mutate(million_reads = reads_processed/1e6, study_name = factor(study_name))
```

## Supplementary Figure `r suppFigIndx` - Prevalence and detection filters

Two options are possible: one global and one per-dataset prevalence and abundance
filter.

The per-dataset prevalence results in fewer features, because some datasets have
very few samples. This would lead to an unfairly strict filter. 

```{r}
preval_curve.df <- data.frame(
  preval_thr = seq(0, 0.9, 0.005),
  nFeatures = sapply(seq(0, 0.9, 0.005), function(thr) {
    return(nrow(subsetByPrevalent(Input_parkinson_usableDatasets.tse, assay.type = "relative_abundance", prevalence = thr, detection = 0)))  
})
)

prevalence_curve.gg <- preval_curve.df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = preval_thr*100, y = nFeatures)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(aes(group =1)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 5, color = "red2") + 
  labs(
    title = "Prevalence curve flattens at 5% prevalence",
    subtitle = "Prevalence threshold of 5% was chosen",
    y = "N Features retained by filter",
    x = "Prevalence (%)"
  )

#--------------------------- same test but with detection

detect_curve.df <- data.frame(
  detection_thr = 10^-c(8:1),
  nFeatures = sapply(10^-c(8:1), function(thr) {
    return(nrow(subsetByPrevalent(Input_parkinson_usableDatasets.tse, assay.type = "relative_abundance", prevalence = 0, detection = thr)))  
})
)

detection_curve.gg <- detect_curve.df %>% 
  # x on the same [0-1] scale as the threshold used in subsetByPrevalent
  ggplot(aes(x = detection_thr, y = nFeatures)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(aes(group =1)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1e-5, color = "red2") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "Detection thresholds",
    subtitle = "A low detection threshold of 1e-5 was chosen",
    y = "N Features retained by filter",
    x = "Detection minimum abundance ([0-1])"
  )

preval_detect_plots.gg <- ggarrange(prevalence_curve.gg, detection_curve.gg, labels = c("a", "b"))


ggsave(plot = preval_detect_plots.gg, filename = sprintf("%s/SupplementaryFigure %s-Prevalence and detection thresholds.svg", outdir, suppFigIndx), height =4.5, width = 9)
saveRDS(preval_detect_plots.gg, file = sprintf("%s/SupplementaryFigure %s-Prevalence and detection thresholds.rds", outdir, suppFigIndx))
```

```{r, fig.height=6, fig.width=11}
preval_detect_plots.gg
```

**Supplementary figure `r suppFigIndx`. Choice of prevalence and detection thresholds for feature filtering.** Number of SGBs retained in the PD-control data (9 datasets, 1,625 samples) as a function of (a) the minimum prevalence, i.e. the percentage of samples in which a SGB is detected, and (b) the minimum relative abundance for a SGB to be considered detected (log10 scale). Prevalence was computed across all samples pooled. Red lines mark the thresholds applied in the analyses: 5% prevalence, where the curve in (a) flattens, and a relative abundance of 10⁻⁵. Samples with fewer than 2 million reads were 
excluded beforehand.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
suppFigIndx <- suppFigIndx + 1
```

## Supplementary figure `r suppFigIndx` - read depth by PD-Control status

Read depth is right-skewed and differs by orders of magnitude between datasets,
so it is analyzed on the `log10` scale: effects are ratios of geometric mean
depths (PD / Control). Per dataset, `lm(log10(reads) ~ parkinson_for_analysis)`
estimates the log10 ratio and its SE; the ratios are pooled with the same
random-effects model used in the meta-analyses (REML, Knapp-Hartung).

A non-significant difference does not prove the absence of a difference, so
equivalence is tested formally (TOST) against a margin of ±10% depth: the
pooled ratio is equivalent if its 90% CI lies within the margin.

Low-depth samples (< 2M reads) are where rare SGBs drop out, so their number is
reported per dataset and group.

```{r read depth equivalence}
depth_threshold <- 2e6
# equivalence margin: PD/Control depth ratio within [1/1.1, 1.1], i.e. ±10%
equivalence_margin <- log10(1.1)

depth.df <- data_for_plot.df %>%
  filter(!is.na(reads_processed)) %>%
  mutate(log10_reads = log10(reads_processed))

# per-dataset log10 ratio of depths, PD vs Control
per_study_depth.df <- depth.df %>%
  group_by(study_name) %>%
  group_modify(function(x, ...) {
    fit <- lm(log10_reads ~ parkinson_for_analysis, data = x)
    coefs <- summary(fit)$coefficients["parkinson_for_analysisPD", ]
    ci <- confint(fit)["parkinson_for_analysisPD", ]
    tibble(
      n_Control = sum(x$parkinson_for_analysis == "Control"),
      n_PD      = sum(x$parkinson_for_analysis == "PD"),
      Beta      = coefs[["Estimate"]],
      SE        = coefs[["Std. Error"]],
      CI.L      = ci[[1]],
      CI.R      = ci[[2]],
      P.Value   = coefs[["Pr(>|t|)"]]
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(P.Value.adj = p.adjust(P.Value, method = "BH"))

# pooled ratio, same random-effects model as the meta-analyses
pooled_depth <- metafor::rma(yi = per_study_depth.df$Beta, sei = per_study_depth.df$SE,
                             method = "REML", test = "knha")

# TOST equivalence test on the pooled estimate (t distribution, Knapp-Hartung df)
tost_p <- max(
  pt((pooled_depth$beta[[1]] + equivalence_margin) / pooled_depth$se, df = pooled_depth$ddf, lower.tail = FALSE),
  pt((pooled_depth$beta[[1]] - equivalence_margin) / pooled_depth$se, df = pooled_depth$ddf, lower.tail = TRUE)
)
ci90 <- pooled_depth$beta[[1]] + c(-1, 1) * qt(0.95, pooled_depth$ddf) * pooled_depth$se

pooled_depth.df <- tibble(
  study_name  = "Pooled (random effects)",
  Beta        = pooled_depth$beta[[1]],
  SE          = pooled_depth$se,
  CI.L        = pooled_depth$ci.lb,
  CI.R        = pooled_depth$ci.ub,
  CI90.L      = ci90[1],
  CI90.R      = ci90[2],
  P.Value     = pooled_depth$pval,
  I2          = pooled_depth$I2,
  Het.Pval    = pooled_depth$QEp,
  TOST.P.Value = tost_p
)

# ratios on the natural scale for the tables
to_ratio <- function(df) mutate(df, across(any_of(c("Beta", "CI.L", "CI.R", "CI90.L", "CI90.R")), ~ 10^.x, .names = "ratio_{.col}"))

per_study_depth.df %>%
  to_ratio() %>%
  select(study_name, n_Control, n_PD, ratio_Beta, ratio_CI.L, ratio_CI.R, P.Value, P.Value.adj) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Per-dataset ratio of geometric mean read depth (PD / Control)")

pooled_depth.df %>%
  to_ratio() %>%
  select(study_name, ratio_Beta, ratio_CI.L, ratio_CI.R, ratio_CI90.L, ratio_CI90.R, P.Value, I2, Het.Pval, TOST.P.Value) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("Pooled ratio; TOST equivalence margin: [%.3f, %.3f]",
                                      10^-equivalence_margin, 10^equivalence_margin))
```

```{r read depth plot}
# A: per-dataset depth distributions (log scale) with BH-adjusted per-dataset P
p_labels.df <- depth.df %>%
  group_by(study_name) %>%
  summarise(y = max(reads_processed) * 1.6 / 1e6, .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(per_study_depth.df, by = "study_name") %>%
  mutate(label = format_p_value(P.Value.adj, digits = 1))

reads_boxplots.gg <- ggplot(depth.df, aes(x = study_name, y = million_reads, color = parkinson_for_analysis)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = depth_threshold / 1e6, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = p_labels.df, aes(x = study_name, y = y, label = label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3, angle = 90) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_color_manual(values = pd_color_palette) +
  labs(
    color = NULL,
    x = NULL,
    y = "Million reads per sample (log10 scale)"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1), legend.position = "top")

# B: forest plot of depth ratios with the equivalence margin
forest.df <- bind_rows(
  per_study_depth.df %>% mutate(type = "Dataset"),
  pooled_depth.df %>% mutate(type = "Pooled")
) %>%
  mutate(study_name = factor(study_name, levels = rev(c(levels(depth.df$study_name), "Pooled (random effects)"))))

reads_forest.gg <- ggplot(forest.df, aes(y = study_name, x = 10^Beta, xmin = 10^CI.L, xmax = 10^CI.R)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 10^-equivalence_margin, xmax = 10^equivalence_margin,
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.15, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  geom_errorbar(width = 0.2) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = type, size = type)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Dataset = 16, Pooled = 18), guide = "none") +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(Dataset = 2, Pooled = 4), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Read depth ratio PD / Control (95% CI)",
    y = NULL,
    caption = sprintf("Shaded: ±10%% equivalence margin. Pooled ratio = %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]; I² = %.0f%%; TOST P = %s",
                      10^pooled_depth$beta[[1]], 10^pooled_depth$ci.lb, 10^pooled_depth$ci.ub,
                      pooled_depth$I2, format_p_value(tost_p, digits = 2))
  )

reads_vs_dataset_color_PD <- ggarrange(reads_boxplots.gg, reads_forest.gg, ncol = 2, labels = c("a", "b"), widths = c(1.2, 1))

# save plot and tables
ggsave(plot = reads_vs_dataset_color_PD, filename = sprintf("%s/SupplementaryFigure %s-Read-depth-by-dataset-and-PD.svg", outdir, suppFigIndx), height = 6, width = 12)
saveRDS(reads_vs_dataset_color_PD, file = sprintf("%s/SupplementaryFigure %s-Read-depth-by-dataset-and-PD.rds", outdir, suppFigIndx))
write_tsv(bind_rows(per_study_depth.df, pooled_depth.df),
          file = sprintf("%s/SupplementaryFigure %s-Read-depth-ratios.tsv", outdir, suppFigIndx))

reads_vs_dataset_color_PD
```

**Supplementary figure `r suppFigIndx`. Sequencing depth of PD and control samples.** (a) Number of reads per sample (millions, log10 scale) in each dataset, by PD/control status. Values above each dataset are Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values (FDR) from a per-dataset linear model of log10(reads) on PD/control status. The dashed line marks 2 million reads, the minimum depth required for a sample to be included. (b) Ratio of the geometric mean depth of PD to control samples, with 95% confidence intervals, for each dataset (circles) and pooled across datasets (diamond). Per-dataset estimates from (a) were pooled with the same random-effects model used for the main meta-analysis (REML with Knapp-Hartung adjustment). The shaded area marks the ±10% equivalence margin (ratio between 0.91 and 1.10). I²: proportion of variability due to heterogeneity between datasets. TOST P: p-value of the two one-sided tests for equivalence; values below 0.05 indicate that the pooled ratio lies within the equivalence margin.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
suppFigIndx <- suppFigIndx + 1
```

## Supplementary Figure `r suppFigIndx` - Beta diversity, unconstrained PCoA (Bray-Curtis)

Unconstrained counterpart of Figure 1c: principal coordinates of Bray-Curtis
dissimilarities on relative abundances, without removing the study effect.

```{r PCoA bray}
Input_parkinson_usableDatasets.tse <- addMDS(Input_parkinson_usableDatasets.tse, assay.type = "relative_abundance", method = "bray", name = "PCoA_bray")

# % explained over positive eigenvalues (Bray-Curtis is not Euclidean)
eigenvalues <- attr(reducedDim(Input_parkinson_usableDatasets.tse, "PCoA_bray"), "eig")
prop_variances_explained <- eigenvalues[eigenvalues > 0] / sum(eigenvalues[eigenvalues > 0])

pcoa_data.df <- cbind.data.frame(
  as.data.frame(colData(Input_parkinson_usableDatasets.tse)),
  reducedDim(Input_parkinson_usableDatasets.tse, "PCoA_bray") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    set_names(paste("MDS", 1:ncol(.)))
)

PCoA_plot_col_parkinson <- pcoa_data.df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = `MDS 1`, y = `MDS 2`, fill = parkinson_for_analysis, color = parkinson_for_analysis)) +
  geom_point(pch = 21, size = 2.5, stroke = 0.5, color = "black") +
  stat_ellipse(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pd_color_palette, aesthetics = c("color", "fill")) +
  labs(color = NULL,
       fill = NULL,
       x = paste0("PCoA Axis 1 [", round(prop_variances_explained[1] * 100, 1), "%]"),
       y = paste0("PCoA Axis 2 [", round(prop_variances_explained[2] * 100, 1), "%]")
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0, 1),
    legend.justification = c(0, 1),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = alpha("white", 0.7), color = "gray50")
  )

# save plot
ggsave(plot = PCoA_plot_col_parkinson, filename = file.path(outdir, sprintf("SupplementaryFigure %s-PCoA-Bray-Curtis-by-PD.svg", suppFigIndx)), height = 6, width = 6)
saveRDS(PCoA_plot_col_parkinson, file = file.path(outdir, sprintf("SupplementaryFigure %s-PCoA-Bray-Curtis-by-PD.rds", suppFigIndx)))

suppFigIndx <- suppFigIndx + 1
PCoA_plot_col_parkinson
```
